title: How Time Travel Works (Live at SD Comic-Con)
summary: Live recording at San Diego Comic-Con 2012 of Stuff You Should Know on how time travel works. The hosts open with banter about the live crowd, then cover Andrew Basiago's claimed participation in a supposed DARPA time travel program (Project Pegasus) as an unverified single-source story, and the physics: relativity and speed-based time travel to the future (Stephen Hawking's essay and the speed-of-light math, with Josh correcting Hawking's figure), Carl Sagan's three reasons we aren't visited by time travelers, GPS satellite time dilation, gravitational time dilation near black holes (Sagittarius A*, spaghettification), exotic objects (the Kerr/"carring" black hole, white holes, Einstein-Rosen bridge/wormholes), and paradoxes (grandfather paradox, consistent causal loops with Back to the Future and Johnny B. Goode, Paul Davies' math professor example, many-worlds theory). A brief fake time-message bit from John Hodgman is included. The episode ends with audience Q&A and a plug for the podcast's books and contact channels.
topics: Back to the Future Johnny B. Goode

segments.title: Opening banter and live recording setup
segments.summary: The hosts introduce the live podcast recorded at San Diego Comic-Con, mention the show's website and upcoming Science Channel appearance, and set up the time travel topic.

segments.title: Andrew Basiago and claimed government time travel program
segments.summary: Josh introduces Seattle attorney Andrew Basiago, who since 2004 has claimed he took part in Project Pegasus, a supposed DARPA time travel initiative using children; they note he is the only source and describe his claimed trips to Gettysburg in 1863 and to Ford's Theatre at the Lincoln assassination, based on claimed technology from Nikola Tesla's papers.

segments.title: Time travel as a philosophical question and future travel by speed
segments.summary: The hosts note that physicists say travel to the future is possible, discuss time as a river and the question of reversing or speeding its flow, and tell a joke about a scientist and philosopher. They then describe Stephen Hawking's essay on time travel and its speed claims, and Josh's correction of Hawking's math about approaching the speed of light.

segments.title: Relativistic travel math and fuel problems
segments.summary: The hosts walk through the fuel and acceleration problem for a ship nearing light speed, including years of acceleration and how time runs differently on the ship relative to Earth. They note that time travel only matters if there is someone to show it to.

segments.title: Carl Sagan and the skeptics' question
segments.summary: The hosts describe the skeptics' question of why time travelers have not visited us, then read Carl Sagan's three possibilities: travel only into the future, travel to our era not yet reached, and backward travel limited to after invention, plus a gloomy option that civilization destroys itself first.

segments.title: Fake John Hodgman time message
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck perform a comedic bit in which a 'time pilot' John Hodgman sends a message from the future warning about trouble at Comic-Con, including references to John Sweden, Firefly, and a Wookie costume.

segments.title: Time travel methods: GPS satellites and gravitational time dilation
segments.summary: The hosts describe traveling to the future and cite GPS satellites, which gain a small amount of time each day because time passes faster in orbit. They explain gravitational time dilation from Earth's mass and describe gravitational lensing near Sagittarius A*, with spaghettification at a black hole.

segments.title: Exotic objects: rotating black holes, white holes, and wormholes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss a rotating black hole formed by neutron stars that avoids a singularity, a possible white hole on the other side, and the Einstein-Rosen bridge, also called a wormhole, illustrated with a folded-sheet analogy.

segments.title: Paradoxes and consistent causal loops
segments.summary: The hosts explain causality and the grandfather paradox, then present the consistent causal loop idea with Paul Davies' math professor example. Brian reads an explanation using Back to the Future and Johnny B. Goode, and the hosts mention Somewhere in Time. They close the topic with the many-worlds parallel universe idea.

segments.title: Summation and audience Q&A
segments.summary: The hosts summarize that time travel's possibility is uncertain but worth asking about. They take audience questions about Celebrity Jeopardy and whether they will publish books.

segments.title: Sign-off and contact information
segments.summary: The hosts give contact channels for the show, including Twitter, Facebook, and email, and sign off.
